The [gSASRec study](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.07192) reports 128-negative gBCE training taking 58 versus 32 minutes for single-negative BCE on Steam, and 191 versus 145 minutes on Gowalla: approximately 1.81× and 1.32×. Steam convergence required 238 versus 170 epochs. MovieLens’s 23 versus 13 minutes used **256**, not 128, negatives. These are dataset-specific convergence times, not transferable per-epoch multipliers. More negatives increase computation and memory, but the paper provides no matched peak-memory ratio for 128 versus one negative. Implementation inference: materializing negative embeddings scales as B×L×K×D; total GPU memory need not increase 128-fold. Profile actual step time and peak memory before budgeting; calibration near t=1 can delay learning.

For this fixed benchmark, recommended uncertainty analysis: retain paired per-user hit indicators, bootstrap users **within each category**, apply identical resampled indices to both models, and recompute the four-category macro difference for a 95% interval. Report category differences and discordant hit counts; one changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points/category or 0.125 points/macro. Such intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidates, excluding training-seed and candidate-sampling variability. [Paired retrieval-evaluation research](https://ciir-publications.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=744) supports bootstrap/randomization approaches. Sampled HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog superiority: [sampled metrics can reverse model rankings](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651).

Predeclare checkpoint frequency, patience, epoch/budget limits, and tie-breaking; select consistently by macro validation HR@10. Count checkpoints alongside variants as selection opportunities. Use Holm-adjusted planned comparisons, but treat post-selection intervals as exploratory: multiplicity adjustment does not remove adaptive selection optimism. Keep held-out evaluation untouched until selection is frozen, as motivated by [model-selection bias research](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).
